issues.feedback: AC3/AC2 implicitly target a truly empty directory, but `ralph daemon start` still requires an existing workspace (`.ralph`) and a local filesystem path. Add explicit preconditions (workspace initialized locally) or include daemon workspace auto-init in scope.

AC6 ('push-and-PR flow succeeds') is stronger than the proposed implementation. Skipping push when `origin` is missing does not satisfy AC6, and brand-new remotes with no default/base branch can still make `gh pr create` fail. Define conditional success criteria or add base-branch bootstrap behavior.

`git commit --allow-empty` can fail under common setups (missing/partial identity, commit hooks, `commit.gpgsign=true`). The spec should mandate a deterministic bootstrap commit path (explicit identity plus no-sign/no-verify behavior) and include a test where global git config is absent.

`has_diff()` currently falls back to `HEAD~1` when base-branch detection fails; with a single bootstrap commit this can be interpreted as 'changes' due to command error. In bootstrapped repos with nonstandard default branches/no origin, this may trigger incorrect push/PR attempts. Address or explicitly scope out this case.

The proposed daemon tests are not fully actionable with current harness defaults (`RalphHarness` always creates a repo with an initial commit). Specify how tests will create non-git and zero-commit states (harness extension or explicit setup), and add a conformance test that exercises AC6 on a truly new remote/base-branch scenario.
